text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 108:
Uniform reciprocating rectilinear motion from uniform rotary motion of a cylinder, in which are cut reverse threads or grooves, which necessarily intersect twice in every revolution. A point inserted in the groove will traverse the cylinder from end to end.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 108; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_108.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 109:
The rotation of the screw at the left-hand side produces a uniform rectilinear movement of a cutter which cuts another screw thread. The pitch of the screw to be cut may be varied by changing the sizes of the wheels at the end of the frame.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 109; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_109.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 110:
Uniform circular into uniform rectilinear motion; used in spooling-frames for leading or guiding the thread on to the spools. The roller is divided into two parts, each having a fine screw thread cut upon it, one a right and the other a left hand screw. The spindle parallel with the roller has arms which carry two half-nuts, fitted to the screws, one over and the other under the roller. When one half-nut is in, the other is out of gear. By pressing the lever to the right or left, the rod is made to traverse in either direction.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 110; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_110.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 112:
Persian drill. The stock of the drill has a very quick thread cut upon it and revolves freely, supported by the head at the top, which rests against the body. The button or nut shown on the middle of the screw is held firm in the hand, and pulled quickly up and down the stock, thus causing it to revolve to the right and left alternately.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 112; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_112.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 151:
Continuous circular into continuous but much slower rectilinear motion. The worm on the upper shaft, acting on the toothed wheel on the screw-shaft, causes the right and left hand screw-threads to move the nuts, upon them toward or from each other according to the direction of rotation.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 151; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_151.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 190:
A screw-clamp. On turning the handle the screw thrusts upward against the holder, which, operating as a lever, holds down the piece of wood or other material placed under it on the other side of its fulcrum.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 190; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_190.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 266:
The shaft has two screws of different pitches cut on it, one screwing into a fixed bearing, and the other into a bearing free to move to and fro. Rotary motion of the shaft gives rectilinear motion to the movable bearing, a distance equal to the difference of pitches, at each revolution.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 266; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_266.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 275:
Rotary motion of the worm gives a rectilinear motion to the rack.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 275; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_275.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 285:
By turning the wheel to the right, motion is communicated to the screw, producing rectilinear motion of the spindle in the end of which the center is fixed.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 285; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_285.html.
